papers.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
papers.summary: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and give examples of smooth connected spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.

papers.title: Lifting mod $p$ Galois representations over local fields
papers.summary: Let $K$ be a local field with absolute Galois group $G_{K}$ and let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$. We prove that every continuous representation $G_K\to \operatorname{GL}_{n}(k)$ lifts to a continuous representation $G_K\to\operatorname{GL}_{n}(W(k))$ where $W(k)$ is the ring of infinite Witt vectors over $k$.

papers.title: Computations in weight 3 of higher Bloch groups
papers.summary: We computationally investigate a weight 3 analogue of the relationship between higher Bloch groups, algebraic K-theory, higher regulators, and special values of Dedekind zeta functions. In particular, for F a number field F, we define the pruned Bloch group B _3(F) and compare the covolume of its regulator lattice with zeta_F(3). We define a quantity kappa_3(F), which is conjecturally an integer, that is expected to be closely related to the order of K_4(O_F).

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
papers.summary: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact Kähler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.

papers.title: Degeneration of (-1)-shifted symplectic stacks and categorification of Donaldson-Thomas invariants
papers.summary: We study cohomological Donaldson-Thomas invariants of perfect complexes in a semistable degeneration of projective Calabi-Yau threefolds, with smooth components $X_1,X_2$ meeting along a smooth anticanonical surface $S$. The generic fiber of degeneration family is a $(-1)$-shifted symplectic stack. Over the special fiber, the derived restriction to $S$ is derived Lagrangian, and its homotopy fiber product is also $(-1)$-shifted symplectic. Our goal is to relate the categorical DT invariants of the generic fiber moduli, induced by periodic cyclic homology of matrix factorization category of 0-shifted potential functions over such moduli, to that of the special fiber obtained via derived Lagrangian intersection and geometric quantization. This is achieved via construction of a flat Gauss-Manin connection that relates the generic fiber cohomological DT invariants to that of the special fiber. The geometric framework, universal trace diagrams, and fourfold foliation were developed jointly with Jacob Kryczka in arXiv:2510.20325. Here we construct ordinary critical realizations, oriented cyclic-to-bar comparisons, and Gauss-Manin operators, and verify finite specialization in explicit moduli problems. We workout our construction via several explicit examples such as Grassmannians, Relative Hilbert Schemes and moduli space of pure 2 dimensional sheaves with support moving in a fixed linear system of divisors in the ambient threefold.

papers.title: Stable homotopy theory of higher categories with adjoints
papers.summary: We demonstrate that higher categories with adjoints behave like homotopy types. By the homotopy hypothesis, homotopy types can be regarded as higher categories in which all cells are invertible. We show that replacing invertibility by the existence of higher adjoints still supports a homotopy theory that is at least as rich as classical homotopy theory. The basic invariants of this theory are the homotopy monoidal categories \[ Π_n(X,x)=\operatorname{Ho}\bigl(Ω^n(X,x)\bigr) \] associated to a based $(\infty,\infty)$-category with adjoints $(X,x)$. These invariants are monoidal categories with duals and replace iterated loops with iterated endomorphisms. The classical homotopy groups of the classifying space are recovered as the isomorphism classes of objects in the groupoid completion. We prove a Whitehead theorem for homotopy monoidal categories and show that fibrations of higher categories give rise to long oriented exact sequences of homotopy monoidal categories. To develop homological algebra of higher categories with adjoints, we prove an equivalence between skeletal sequences of categorical spectra with adjoints and categorical chain complexes, extending a result outlined by Lurie in the proof of the cobordism hypothesis.

papers.title: Sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen-Macaulay schemes
papers.summary: In this paper, we prove a sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen-Macaulay schemes of pure dimension over an arbitrary field. In particular, if L is an ample line bundle on a smooth complex projective variety X and J is a coherent ideal sheaf with J\otimes L globally generated, then (\sqrt{J})^{°_L X}\subseteq J. This establishes the sharp bound conjectured by Ein and Lazarsfeld. More generally, we obtain sharp bounds in terms of mixed intersection numbers and a refinement involving products of powers of prime ideal sheaves associated to the irreducible components of the base locus. We also establish sharp radical power bounds for homogeneous ideals in finitely generated standard graded Cohen-Macaulay domains, extending Kollár's sharp effective Nullstellensatz for polynomial rings. The proofs combine purity and cycle preservation for leading Ext sheaves with Koszul evaluation maps compatible with successive divisor cuts.

papers.title: ACM, almost Ulrich, and Ulrich vector bundles arising from Frobenius
papers.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We investigate ACM, almost Ulrich (both ACM and weakly Ulrich), and Ulrich properties of the sheaves of locally exact and closed $i$-forms $B_X^i$, $Z_X^i$. These cohomological properties are closely related to the fundamental concepts of Frobenius splitting and ordinarity. Joshi studied the sheaf $B^1_X$ in this context in \cite{MR3920911, MR4206787}, including ACM and almost Ulrich twists of $B^1_X$. However, varieties with Ulrich twisted $B_X^1$ have not been classified for $n\ge2$. We classify subcanonical polarized varieties with initialized ACM $B^i_X(aH)$ for $i=1, n$ and prove that, for $n \ge 2$, varieties with ACM $B^i_X$ for all $i \le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil$ are ordinary. When $X$ is ordinary with trivial $Ω^1_X$, almost Ulrich twists of $B^i_X$ and $F_*^e(Z_X^i(aH))$ are determined. We classify polarized varieties $(X,H)$ with $B_X^i(aH)$ Ulrich when $n=1, 2$, and establish strong necessary criteria for $n \geq 3$, together with an example. We also prove that $Z_X^i(aH)$ is never Ulrich. Finally, we classify polarized abelian varieties with Ulrich $B^1_X \otimes L$ allowing twists by arbitrary line bundles.

papers.title: Voevodsky's motives and zeroth slice of motivic sphere
papers.summary: Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension and let $R$ be a commutative ring in which every positive residue characteristic of $S$ is invertible. We prove that Voevodsky's stable Nisnevich category of motives with $R$-coefficients is canonically equivalent to modules over the zeroth slice of the motivic sphere with derived $R$-coefficients. The comparison identifies the corresponding commutative coefficient algebras and is compatible with arbitrary pullback. The theorem applies to singular and nonreduced schemes, including mixed-characteristic bases, and requires no excellence or finite-type hypothesis. Its special cases include rational coefficients over arbitrary bases, arbitrary coefficients over $\mathbb Q$-schemes, and $\mathbb Z[1/p]$-algebra coefficients over $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-schemes. The proof establishes base change for finite-cycle spectra using permutation quotients, families of cycles, and arithmetic power homotopies, then passes to general bases by universal homeomorphism invariance and continuity.

papers.title: Aspects of quadratic Chabauty via modular forms
papers.summary: We develop algorithms to construct a basis of de Rham cohomology for modular curves and a matrix representing the Hodge filtration required in the quadratic Chabauty method. We do this without requiring an explicit plane model of the curve and instead compute these objects in terms of modular forms. Our approach works for any modular curve; to demonstrate its efficiency, we implement our method for nonsplit Cartan modular curves.

papers.title: Quasi locally free sheaves on primitive double schemes
papers.summary: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $U$ of $X_2$ and integers $m_1$, $m_2$, uniquely determined by $E$, such that $E_{|U}$ is locally isomorphic to $(O_X\otimes C^{m_1})\oplus(O_{X_2}\otimes C^{m_2})$. If we can take $U=X_2$, we say the $E$ is quasi locally free. If $m_1=1$ we say that $E$ is rigid. In this case, we show that deformations of $E$ are of the same type. So locally free sheaves and rigid quasi locally free sheaves on $X_2$ play the same role on $X_2$ as locally free sheaves do on smooth schemes. In this paper we study the existence and description of quasi locally free sheaves, and flat families of such sheaves.

papers.title: Day Convolution and Homotopy Groups on the Pointed Homotopy Category of CW Complexes
papers.summary: We freely enrich the pointed homotopy category of CW complexes over abelian groups and equip the resulting functor category with the enriched Day convolution induced by the smash product. After identifying the convolution unit and recording the coherence maps, we compute the convolution of the homotopy-group functors. For integers $n,m\geq 2$ we construct a natural isomorphism $π_n\starπ_m\congπ_{n+m}$ induced by the external smash product; equivalently, the external smash product is the universal natural pairing of homotopy groups. Under this identification, the symmetry interchanging the two factors acts on $π_{n+m}$ by multiplication by $(-1)^{nm}$.

papers.title: Delta Characters and Ranks of Minimal Subisocrystals of Abelian Schemes
papers.summary: Using the framework of delta characters on arithmetic jet spaces, we construct a canonical sequence of filtered isocrystals associated to an abelian scheme $A$ of relative dimension $g$ over a $p$-adically complete discrete valuation ring. These isocrystals map injectively via a canonical morphism into the first (rational) crystalline cohomology group $\mathbf{H}^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A)$ of the abelian scheme $A$, directly generalizing a prior construction due to Borger and Saha. Pandit showed that the canonical morphism is a map of isocrystals. This then implies that the image of this canonical embedding coincides with the minimal subisocrystal $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ containing the space of invariant differential forms $H^0(A,Ω_A)$. Berthelot and Ogus showed that the dimension of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ is $g$ if and only if $A$ has an endomorphism that lifts the absolute Frobenius on the special fiber of $A$. As a primary application, for a general abelian scheme $A$, we show that the minimal subisocrystal $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ can be viewed as a module obtained from primitive delta characters of $A$ via appropriate twists by the canonical Frobenius morphism $φ$ induced from the theory of arithmetic jet spaces. As a consequence, we show that the rank of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ depends on numerical invariants arising from the theory of delta characters of $A$. More precisely, the dimension of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ is given by the sum of the exact orders of the primitive delta characters associated to the abelian scheme $A$.

papers.title: Isogenies of Oriented Elliptic Curves
papers.summary: We construct and describe the moduli stack $\mathrm{Isog}$ of isogenies between oriented elliptic curves. We show that $\mathrm{Isog}$ is a spectral Deligne-Mumford stack and a relative spectral algebraic space over $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}^{\mathrm{or}}$, and give a fiber product decomposition of $\mathrm{Isog}$ corresponding to a connected-étale factorization on oriented elliptic curves. In the process of proving these results, we construct a theory of duality and quotients for spectral abelian varieties, prove a higher-algebraic version of Nakayama's lemma, and lift the rigidity theorem for morphisms of elliptic curves to the setting of spectral algebraic geometry.

papers.title: Explicit Serre weights for modular Galois representations of $U(2)$
papers.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $F$ be a totally imaginary CM field and $F^+$ be the maximal totally real subfield such that $F/F^+$ is unramified at all finite places, and every place $v | p$ of $F^+$ is split in $F$. We allow arbitrary ramification of $p$ in $F^+$. Let $G$ be a rank two definite unitary group over $F^+$ as defined in [2]. Fix a place $\mathfrak{p} | p$ in $F$. In this article, we determine explicit local Serre weights at $\mathfrak{p}$ attached to a modular mod $p$ Galois representation $\barρ_h$ of the absolute Galois group of $F$, associated to an eigenform $h$ of $G$. The eigenform $h$ has arbitrary weights and small slope at $\mathfrak{p}$. We also show analogous results for certain Hilbert modular eigenforms with arbitrary ramification of $p$ in the totally real field. The eigenforms come from totally definite and indefinite quaternion algebras over totally real fields, split at places above $p$. In proving our results, we identify the non-singular submodules in quotients of certain symmetric power $\mathbb{F}_q[\text{M}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$-modules by Dickson polynomials and their twisted versions.

papers.title: On equivariant affineness in elliptic cohomology
papers.summary: We investigate equivariant affineness in spectral algebraic geometry: the phenomenon where $\infty$-categories of quasi-coherent sheaves of a spectral stack are equivalent to $\infty$-categories of modules over an equivariant ring spectrum. In the nonequivariant case, this is known as 0-affineness, and has been studied by Gaitsgory, Mathew--Meier, amongst others. Allowing for equivariant phenomena opens up a much wider class of spectral stacks to be studied through the lens of spectra. The spectral stacks at the heart of our analysis are oriented elliptic curves, their associated Hilbert schemes, and related constructions. When working over the universal base, so the moduli stack of oriented elliptic curves, we show that these spectral stacks are $U(1)$-, $U(n)$-, and $SU(n)$-equivariantly affine, with associated $G$-ring spectrum Gepner--Meier's equivariant topological modular forms $\mathrm{TMF}_G$. Our results also encompass the groups $Sp(n)$ as well as all finite products of such groups. Our most general result is a relative statement over an arbitrary base stack. These results can be viewed as an integral and global refinement of Greenlees' algebraic model for modules over rational $U(1)$-equivariant elliptic cohomology.

papers.title: Sheaves on nodal singularities I
papers.summary: We study two families of moduli spaces of sheaves attached to the node, namely the punctual Hilbert schemes of the non-reduced plane curve $x^uy^v=0$, and the punctual Quot schemes of the module $k[[x]]^u\oplus k[[y]]^v$ over the reduced node $xy=0$. We compute their motivic generating functions for all $u,v$ and over every field. Both are specializations of a single rational function whose numerator counts matrices by rank, and they are related by the substitution $\mathbb{L}\mapsto Q\mathbb{L}$. This proves the Hilb--Quot correspondence for the node with independent ranks on the two branches. The main geometric ingredient is an elementary modification of an ideal along a branch of the curve, whose fibres are affine spaces of dimension equal to a contact length. We also construct stratifications of the Hilbert schemes into products of affine spaces and tori, and we formulate a branchwise Hilb--Quot--HOMFLY conjecture, which we test on the colored Hopf link.

papers.title: The Segal conjecture for large objects and semiadditive lifts
papers.summary: We prove a projection formula for homotopy fixed points of trivial actions of finite $p$-groups. More precisely, for every bounded-below, $p$-complete spectrum $X$ whose mod-$p$ homology is $I$-complete, the canonical map \[ (\mathbb S_p)^{BG}\otimes X \overset{\simeq}{\rightarrow} X^{BG} \] is an equivalence for every finite $p$-group $G$, where $I$ is the augmentation ideal of the Steenrod algebra. Building on earlier joint work with Burklund, our proof combines the Adams--Gunawardena--Miller calculation with an adaptation of Carlsson's induction. As an application, using the work of Yuan, we construct height-one semiadditive lifts of such spectra and show that their cohomology of $p$-finite spaces depends only on the $1$-type.

papers.title: Galois groups of polynomials over a fixed number field: determinant methods in general boxes, resolvents, and quantitative counting
papers.summary: Let $K$ be a fixed number field of degree $d$. We prove two determinant-method results for integral points over $\mathcal O_K$ in boxes whose coordinates may have different size bounds: a Bombieri-Pila type estimate for affine plane curves that retains the two separate coordinate bounds, and a Salberger-Browning covering theorem for affine surfaces. If $F\in\mathcal O_K[X_1,X_2]$ is irreducible and $T=\max B_1^{e_1}B_2^{e_2}$ over the monomials occurring in $F$, then \[ N_K(F;B_1,B_2)\ll T^\varepsilon \exp\!\left(d\frac{\log B_1\log B_2}{\log T}\right). \] For an absolutely irreducible surface in three variables we obtain a covering by $O(T^\varepsilon V_{3,K})$ bounded-degree auxiliary hypersurfaces, outside $O(T^\varepsilon V_{3,K}^2)$ exceptional integral points, where \[ V_{3,K}=\exp\!\left(d \left(\frac{\log B_1\log B_2\log B_3}{\log T}\right)^{1/2}\right). \] These are the number-field analogues of determinant-method estimates for unequal coordinate ranges developed in the rational setting by Browning and Heath-Brown, Salberger, Browning, and Chow-Dietmann. We then apply them to Galois resolvents of monic degree-$n$ polynomials over $K$. Independently, a large-sieve argument, in the tradition of Gallagher's probabilistic Galois theory, gives $O_{K,n}(N^{dn-d/2}\log N)$ exceptional separable polynomials, while effective Hilbert irreducibility over global fields gives subgroup-sensitive bounds with exponent $d(n-1+1/[S_n:G])$, up to logarithms. We record the interaction with the discriminant-square equation for even groups, congruence restrictions, and rectangular coefficient boxes. All determinant estimates used in the applications are proved in the paper; no conjectural global-field determinant statement is assumed.

papers.title: On the motivic approach to the Abhyankar rectifiability problem and concrete rectifications
papers.summary: We study closed embeddings of the complex affine line into affine three-space. We prove that, for every such embedding, the complete-intersection normal map identifies the $\mathbb{A}^1$-fundamental sheaf of its complement with $\mathbf{K}_2^{\mathrm{MW}}$. The proof compares torsors under arbitrary strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves. A nodal projection expresses a torsor by a normal parameter and finitely many node parameters. Extension across the node axes gives equations for the latter. Their correction terms increase a nilpotent filtration generated by the Milnor-Witt symbols of the branch-height differences. We deduce the vanishing of the first Alexander sheaf of every complex embedded line. We also construct polynomial rectifications using finite inverses and affine modifications, including rectifications of the Shastri trefoil and a harmonic figure-eight over $\mathbb{Z}[a]/(a^2-a+1)$, with arbitrary base change. The companion repository (https://github.com/qft98romanov-hash/abhyankar-moh-trefoil) contains explicit rectifiers, their inverses, proofs, and symbolic checks. We prove that a normal map with a polynomial section and geometric generic affine-line fiber is a coordinate projection. We formulate the remaining rectifiability and descent questions; the general complex rectifiability problem is not settled here. An appendix treats other fields, normal orientations, and arithmetic descent.

papers.title: Hartl's dictionary and a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with complex multiplication
papers.summary: We update Hartl's dictionary between $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog to include aspects related to the Hodge--Tate filtration in $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog, the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration. Using this update, we establish a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with abelian Tannakian structure group, matching a result of Howe--Klevdal in the $p$-adic setting. A special case of this result says that a formal Drinfeld module over an equicharacteristic local field has complex multiplication if and only if the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration on its $z$-adic Tate module is algebraic.

papers.title: Deterministic Root-Finding over Finite Fields with Elliptic Curves
papers.summary: Finding the roots of a polynomial over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ in deterministic polynomial time is a long-standing open problem. Classical deterministic methods work in the multiplicative group $\mathbb F_q^\times$ and are efficient only when $q-1$ is smooth, which is rarely the case. We propose a method that replaces $\mathbb F_q^\times$ by the groups of rational points of an elliptic curve $E$ and of its quadratic twist $\widetilde E$. The computation splits into an offline phase, which depends only on $\mathbb F_q$ and outputs a short \emph{elliptic preprocessing datum} $\mathcal D$, and an online phase, which processes the input polynomial. Writing $Ξ(\mathcal D)$ for the largest prime factor of $\lvert E(\mathbb F_q)\rvert\cdot\lvert\widetilde E(\mathbb F_q)\rvert$, the online phase is deterministic and finds the roots of any $f\in\mathbb F_q[X]$ of degree $n$ within $\widetilde O(Ξ(\mathcal D)^2\,n\log^2 q+n^ω\log q+n\log^3 q)$ operations in $\mathbb F_q$. A precursor of our method is an algorithm by Rónyai, which recovers the roots through Galois computations over number fields, relies on GRH, and comes with a polynomial bound of unspecified degree; in contrast, our online phase works entirely over $\mathbb F_q$ and is unconditional. Moreover, $\mathcal D$ can be certified deterministically and unconditionally in time polynomial in $\log q$ and $Ξ(\mathcal D)$. We conjecture that every $\mathbb F_q$ of large enough characteristic admits a datum with $Ξ(\mathcal D)\leq(\log q)^{O(1)}$, and support this with a heuristic and with experiments. Constructing such a datum in polynomial time remains open.

papers.title: Extreme values of Artin $L$-functions at $s=1$
papers.summary: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a Galois extension of number fields with Galois group $G$. Let $χ$ be any character on $G$ and $κ(χ)$ be the leading coefficient of the Laurent series of the Artin $L$-function $L(s,χ)$ at $s=1$. Cho, Lemke Oliver, and Zaman (2026) recently established a conditional bound for $κ(χ)$ assuming GRH for the Dedekind zeta function of $K$. Up to implied constants, we show that the extremal values of these bounds are attained for an infinite family of extensions $K/\mathbb{Q}$ and all irreducible faithful characters $χ$, provided $G$ is a regular Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$. All characters $χ$ are permitted without restriction when $G$ is abelian, $A_n, S_n$, or any sporadic group. Our method removes the assumptions of GRH and Artin's holomorphy conjecture from an argument of Duke (2003) by following the strategy of Lemke Oliver, Thorner, and Zaman (2024) on the existence of extremal class numbers for number fields of arbitrary degree. Key ingredients include progress by Débes (2017) towards Malle's conjecture, and an Artin $L$-function large sieve by Lemke Oliver and Smith (2024).

papers.title: Intrinsic Non-Reductive Geometric Invariant Theory and Moduli Spaces of Principal Bundles with Non-Reductive Structure Groups
papers.summary: We prove the existence of moduli spaces for algebraic stacks with a weak action of $Θ= [\mathbb{A}^1/\mathbb{G}_m]$ (including stacks of filtered objects and unstable $Θ$-strata) for which the center admits a good moduli space and the retraction to the center has flat, finitely presented relative inertia, providing a stack-intrinsic generalization of the existence of non-reductive Geometric Invariant Theory quotients. As an application, we construct quasi-projective coarse moduli spaces of principal bundles over a smooth projective curve with non-reductive structure groups, including moduli spaces of Ramanathan unstable principal bundles of fixed Harder--Narasimhan type.

papers.title: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds
papers.summary: We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang's descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, Kähler--Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture.

papers.title: Alternative moduli of twisted curves
papers.summary: We define new Artin stack compactifications of the moduli of smooth curves, which parameterize "relatively polarized curves" consisting of stacky semistable curves equipped with line bundles that are trivialized away from the rational bridges. Using techniques from birational geometry, we prove that stacks of relatively polarized curves admit the classical coarse space $\overline{M}_g$ of stable curves as a good moduli space. One of our main motivations is a companion paper where we construct a proper moduli space of $\mathrm{SL}_N$-bundles on relatively polarized curves. This suggests the hypothesis that relatively polarized curves are suitable sources for defining Gromov-Witten theory for Artin stack targets.

papers.title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
papers.summary: Let $X=V_5$ be the quintic del Pezzo threefold. Along the negative zero-tilt-slope paths for rational-curve ideal classes, degree five is the first degree admitting a positive point correction. We determine the resulting degree-five outer good moduli space: it is reduced with exactly two irreducible components, a normal ten-dimensional principal branch and a smooth corrected branch $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$. Their scheme-theoretic intersection is a normal determinantal ninefold. Along its singular locus, the principal branch has transverse rank-one $2\times 4$ determinantal singularities, while the intersection has the corresponding $2\times 3$ singularities. We construct an explicit small resolution of the principal branch as the projectivization of a rank-five extension bundle over the blow-up of the Altavilla--Petković--Rota Kuznetsov-component sixfold along its point locus. Uniform wall exclusion and point-correction bounds for degrees two through five establish the first correction threshold; the corrected degree-five factors are precisely the ideals of elliptic linear sections parametrized by $\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$.

papers.title: Leafrians, Frobenius splittings, and moduli spaces over Poisson surfaces
papers.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Poisson surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, and let $s\in H^0(X,ω_X^{-1})$ be nonzero. We construct an anticanonical section associated to $s$, called the leafrian, on moduli spaces $M$ of stable objects on $X$, including the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons. The leafrian splits $M$ if and only if $s^{p-1}$ Frobenius splits the base. It is invariant under the Hamiltonian flows of Bottacin's Poisson structure on $M$, so every compatibly split subvariety of $M$ is a Poisson subvariety. Furthermore, the leafrian extends to an anticanonical section on the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$, and splits $\bar M$ under the same criterion. As a consequence, for $X$ a rational surface, a ruled surface over an elliptic curve, a $K3$ surface, or an abelian surface, and $ρ>0$, the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$ satisfies Kodaira-type cohomology vanishing, including singular $\bar M$, and the same holds in characteristic zero.

papers.title: Rational Points on Affine Varieties over Finite Fields and Polygonal Number Sequences
papers.summary: Authors, in an earlier work, proved that prime power subsequences of the polygonal numbers corresponding to $4$, $6$, $8$, and $10$ arise naturally as the numbers of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points of certain double Danielewski surfaces. In this work, authors generalize the previous construction and give a new family of affine varieties over finite fields such that the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points of these varieties give the prime power subsequence of every polygonal number sequence.

papers.title: Moduli space of irregular singular $λ$-connections and the relative symplectic form
papers.summary: We study the moduli space of $λ$-connections with ramified singularities on a smooth projective curve $X$. We construct a quasi-projective relative moduli scheme $M^α_{\mathrm{Hod}} \to Λ$ of $α$-stable $λ$-connections over a base parameter space $Λ$. This moduli space connects the irregular de Rham moduli space ($λ=1$) and the irregular Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs bundles equipped with non-zero irregular local exponents ($λ=0$). Furthermore, we show that $M^α_{\mathrm{Hod}}$ is smooth over $Λ$ and carries a canonical relative symplectic form $ω_{M^α_{\mathrm{Hod}}/Λ}$, yielding a natural Poisson structure on the total space.

We construct a quasi-projective relative moduli scheme $M^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{Hod}} \to \Lambda$ of $\alpha$-stable $\lambda$-connections over a base parameter space $\Lambda$. papers.title: Log blow-ups and global resolutions in rigid geometry
papers.summary: In this article, we study log blow-ups in the setting of log adic spaces. As in the theory of log schemes, we prove the existence of global resolutions of toric singularities for fs log adic spaces log smooth over a $p$-adic field, and the acyclicity of certain sheaves under log blow-ups. One new feature of (log) rigid analytic varieties is their integral structure sheaf: we prove that it is also almost acyclic under log blow-ups in the Kummer étale topology. We also supply some foundational results on log adic spaces.

papers.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
papers.summary: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials. Applications include cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa distance bounds, rank-metric codes, trace codes, and Fourier support. Character orthogonality and Gauss and Jacobi sums yield counting formulas, a proof of the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field character sums. Gaussian periods connect these methods with short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups. Proofs of Weil bounds for polynomial character sums combine auxiliary polynomials with generating polynomials and estimates for their reciprocal roots. The emphasis throughout is on explicit arguments connecting field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.

papers.title: Some chromatic height computations for homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology
papers.summary: For an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum $R$ of chromatic height $k$, the trace method and the chromatic redshift imply that $T^n$-fixed point of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $R$ has chromatic height at most $k+n$. In this paper, we compute these heights for $H\mathbb{F}_p$, $H\mathbb{Z}$ and the $p$-complete connective image-of-$J$ spectrum $j_p$ for all primes and $n\geq1$, which are exactly $n-1$, $n$ and $n+1$, respectively. Our method is based on properties of Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology over $\mathrm{MU}$.

papers.title: Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson classes of symmetric powers and applications
papers.summary: The Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson class $c_{SM}(X)$ is defined in the Chow group $A_*(X)$ of a scheme $X$, and generalizes $c(T_X)\cap [X]$ if $X$ is smooth. In this paper we independently compute $c_{SM}(S^nX)\in A_*(S^nX)$ modulo $n!$ torsion; we use this result to compute the pushforward to $S^nX$ of $c_{SM}(Quot^n_X(E))$ (and in particular $c_{SM}(Hilb^n X)$) when $X$ is smooth and $E$ is a vector bundle on $X$. Finally, when $X$ is smooth and complete of dimension $3$ we propose a refined version of the the MNOP conjecture that computes the image of the pushforward of $[Hilb^n X]^{vir}$ to $A_0(S^nX)$ and prove it modulo $n!$ torsion when $X$ is Calabi-Yau.

papers.summary: Let $C_{p, 2}(\mathbb{P}^{n})$ denote the Chow variety parametrizing effective algebraic $p$-cycles of degree two on $\mathbb{P}^{n}$. We show that its rational cohomology is pure Tate and concentrated in even degrees. An anti-invariant Chern class identity yields a presentation of the cohomology ring as a fiber product, which in turn determines the cohomology over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$. We identify the ordinary Poincaré polynomial with the known virtual formula, determine the optimal ranges over which the coefficients stabilize, and compute the nonrational Poincaré series of the stable space $D(2)$. For the Lawson--Michelsohn map $D(2)\longrightarrow D(\infty)$, the first nonzero rational homotopy kernel occurs in degree eight and is one-dimensional, while the integral kernel has rank one. Finally, we compute the relative homology of the pair $(D(2),BU)$ over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$ and show that additional cohomology generators and nonzero rational homotopy kernels arise in unbounded degrees.

papers.title: Class numbers and finiteness of norm Euclidean quadratic lattices over algebraic number fields
papers.summary: Let $F$ be an algebraic number field and $\mathcal{O}_{F}$ the ring of integers of $F$. Let $L$ be an integral $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-lattice of rank $n\ge1$ on an anisotropic quadratic space $V$. We prove that if $L$ is norm Euclidean, then $L$ is $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-maximal of class number one, and the class number of $F$ equals the class number of $L\perp\mathbf{H}$, where $\mathbf{H}$ is the hyperbolic lattice with quadratic form $xy$. Under the same assumption, $F$ has class number one if $n\ge3$ and at most two if $n=1,2$. We also prove finiteness up to isometry for totally definite norm Euclidean lattices over totally real number fields in ranks at least three as the field varies, in rank two for fixed field degree, and in rank one over a fixed field. This confirms Clark's finiteness conjecture in ranks at least three.

papers.title: Representations and $n$-universality of hermitian lattices over local and number fields
papers.summary: Let $E/F$ be a quadratic field extension. For any positive integer $n$ an integral hermitian form over $E/F$ is called $n$-universal if it represents all integral hermitian forms of rank $n$ over $E/F$. We study $n$-universal hermitian forms when $F$ is a local field of characteristic $\neq 2$ or a number field. In the local case, we characterize $n$-universal integral hermitian forms and provide finite criterion sets for $n$-universality. In the number field case, we show that an indefinite integral hermitian form is $n$-universal if and only if it is $n$-universal everywhere locally.

papers.title: Power Sum Varieties over Finite Fields
papers.summary: We study a family of affine algebraic varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ defined by systems of power sum polynomials. Our main goal is to investigate their geometric and arithmetic properties, with particular emphasis on the structure and dimension of their singular loci. Using tools from the theory of symmetric polynomials and generalized Vandermonde determinants, we establish explicit conditions under which these varieties are complete intersections and prove that, in a broad range of parameters, their singular loci have codimension at least two. As a consequence, we derive normality and irreducibility results for both the affine varieties and their projective closures. Building on this geometric analysis, we obtain estimates for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and deduce effective existence results for solutions of systems of symmetric power sum equations over finite fields. Finally, we apply these results to the study of Waring's problem and to the analysis of the cost of computing a $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational point of such systems.

papers.title: Meromorphic approximation of holomorphic maps into algebraically elliptic projective varieties
papers.summary: We show that holomorphic maps from a neighborhood of a compact set in a Stein space to an algebraically elliptic smooth projective variety can be approximated by meromorphic maps, provided that the map extends continuously to the whole space and the compact set is convex with respect to a submonoid of the Picard group. The proof uses algebraic sprays and their polynomial lifts to affine cones, which we call conic lifts. Rational sprays, which generalize algebraic sprays, extend the result to maps avoiding the exceptional set of a rational spray. We also show that, for smooth projective varieties, the existence of an algebraic spray which is dominating at some point is a birational invariant.

papers.title: Construction of Galois modules describing ideal class groups and applications to Iwasawa theory
papers.summary: For a finite Galois extension of number fields, the ideal class groups of intermediate fields do not behave well under taking Galois coinvariants in general. papers.title: Number of equations defining the Kummer varieties of hyperelliptic curves
papers.summary: The Jacobian of an hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is equipped with a symmetric theta divisor $Θ$ that defines a principal polarization. As a consequence, we obtain a formula for the number of quartic equations defining $K$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$.

papers.title: Lax descent and foliated Verdier duality
papers.summary: Higher categorical methods allow us to view recollements as lax descent data and build a corresponding descent theory governed by an $\infty$-bicategorical theory of limits. We demonstrate some concrete innovations brought along by these new techniques in the classical context of constructible and perverse sheaves on stratified spaces. Our first application uses partially (op)lax descent to recover the famous result of Beilinson telling us how to glue perverse sheaves in terms of vanishing and nearby cycles. The remainder of the article is concerened with establishing a uniform view on a series of classification results for perverse sheaves culminating in recent work of Kapranov-Schechtman. Namely, we use lax descent to establish a ``foliated'' variant of Verdier duality which, informally speaking, identifies the derived constructible category of a suitably foliated space with sections of a categorical cosheaf on the leaf space whose stalks are the categories of sheaves along the leaves. Again, this is obtained as an application of lax descent, and seems to provide a reasonable framework to formalize the idea of ``mixed sheaf-cosheaf objects'' promoted by Kapranov and Schechtman.

papers.title: Localization of weighted Goldman volume on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\R)$-Hitchin Component
papers.summary: We compute Goldman volume on the moduli space of convex real projective structures on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two, with exponential weight defined by the shifted Blaschke area. For every positive parameter, the integral converges and is a finite sum of inverse powers of that parameter. Its coefficients are intersection numbers involving the bundle of regular cubic differentials on the moduli stack of stable curves. The proof establishes absolute convergence and vanishing signed boundary integrals of the transgression under simultaneous plumbing degeneration. The pushforward of Goldman measure by the shifted Blaschke area therefore has a polynomial density on $[0,\infty)$, and its sublevel volumes are polynomial in the threshold.

papers.title: Spectra, Growth, and Localization in Half-Bounded Tensor Triangular Geometry
papers.summary: Over a noetherian scheme, classical cohomological support determines thick tensor ideals of perfect complexes. In half-bounded derived categories, complexes with the same support can generate different radical thick tensor ideals. We study how these distinctions affect the Balmer spectrum and localization. For a commutative noetherian ring $R$, we prove that $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian. For a nonempty noetherian scheme $X$, the corresponding condition is $\dim X=0$. For such a ring $R$ and a finite group $G$, $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(RG))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian and $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Using the Sanders--Zhang classification over a discrete valuation ring, we compare objects whose annihilator exponents grow at different rates in different degrees. We lift the relevant generation relations before changing coefficients and obtain spectral retractions. These comparisons persist after thick quotients and algebraic localization under explicit uniform annihilation and nonvanishing conditions. A second argument uses nonnilpotent classes of positive degree and passes from cyclic subgroups to finite groups. Applications include relative results for schemes and bounded-below spectra with degreewise finitely generated homotopy. We also describe the cohomological information shared by the resulting ideals. The localization comparisons for bounded-below complexes of finitely generated modules and for bounded-below derived objects with finitely generated cohomology are established separately.

papers.title: Discretisation in algebraic $K$-theory of independent ample groupoids and their Steinberg algebras
papers.summary: An independent ample groupoid $G$ comes equipped with a discrete groupoid $G_d$ and a proper étale correspondence $Ω:G_d\to G$. Discretisation with respect to a homological invariant $\mathcal{H}$ holds when $\mathcal{H}(Ω)$ is an equivalence. We show for example that discretisation with respect to the $K$-theory spectrum $\mathbb{K} \mathfrak{B}_G$ of the permutative category of bisections always holds, establish excision and continuity for this invariant, and use all this and explicit resolutions by independent groupoids to compute it for several families of ample groupoids. We also prove discretisation with respect to invariants of the Steinberg algebra $\ell[G]$ such as (homotopy) algebraic $K$-theory in several particular cases, and carry out computations.

papers.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
papers.summary: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{η_1,\ldots,η_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $η_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{η_i,η_j\in S:η_i\neqη_j}|\mathcal N(η_i-η_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.

papers.title: Spectral zeta functions in positive characteristic
papers.summary: Spectral zeta functions and zeta-regularized determinants encode the spectrum of an operator in analytic functions. Over the completion $\mathbb C_\infty$ of an algebraic closure of $\mathbb F_q((π))$, two features of characteristic $p$ break this classical picture. Complex powers have exponents that vary only continuously in $\mathbb Z_p$, not analytically. Scalar traces record eigenvalue multiplicities only modulo $p$. We develop a resolvent-based theory that treats these two obstructions separately. For the first, inverse Stieltjes duality turns suitable scalar resolvents into locally analytic spectral distributions on $\mathbb F_q[[π]]$. A single exponent of the Mellin transform already determines the distribution and the entire Mellin family. We characterize exactly which power series arise in this way, by a growth condition on Carlitz moments. The criterion depends on the support: bounded Taylor coefficients are not sufficient. For stationary digit measures, the transform is the unique fixed point of an explicit contraction. The first $q-1$ nonconstant moments recover the measure. For the second, we replace traces by the Frobenius defect $F/σ(F)$, where $σ$ raises coefficients to their $q$th powers. On power series with small coefficients, this map is a group automorphism that preserves Gauss distances, and a convergent infinite product inverts it. Polynomial defects produce entire functions. They characterize exactly the diagonal spectra that are finite unions of forward Frobenius orbits, counted with multiplicity. For the shifted Carlitz operator, the resulting Fredholm determinant is a normalized reciprocal of the Anderson--Thakur function, and its Newton polygon is determined exactly.

papers.title: Special cycles and Picard groups of Baily--Borel compactifications
papers.summary: In this paper, we answer two basic questions concerning algebraic cycles on orthogonal Shimura varieties attached to lattices. First, we prove that Kudla's special cycles and Heegner cycles have the same rational span in every codimension. This fills a gap in the codimension-one argument of \cite[Remark 2.4]{BLMM17}, pointed out by Bruinier--Zuffetti \cite{BZ26}. Second, in dimension at least ten, we prove that the rational Picard group of the Baily--Borel compactification is generated by the Hodge class. The proof of the second result reduces, via isotropic induction on the discriminant form, to the K3-type case treated in our previous work.

papers.title: Dimensions of Fano schemes of lines on hypersurfaces
papers.summary: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n_\mathbb{C}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$. We prove that an $m$-dimensional integral projective family of lines sweeping a variety of dimension $y$ satisfies $m\le\max\{2y-d-1,n-3\}$. This proves the de Jong-Debarre conjecture for $d\le n$ and the Beheshti-Starr bound for lines on smooth hypersurfaces for $d\ge n+1$.

papers.title: Fine points of the moduli space of cubic rational maps
papers.summary: A rational point of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_3$ of cubic rational maps is fine if its conjugacy class contains a map defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and coarse otherwise. In the invariants $ξ_0,\dots,ξ_5$ that embed $\mathcal{M}_3$ in $\mathbb{P}(2,2,3,3,4,6)$, we prove that a point with trivial automorphism group is fine if and only if the quaternion algebra $(-m_{12},-2ξ_0)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ splits, where $m_{12}=\frac{1}{3}ξ_0^2ξ_1+ξ_0ξ_4-ξ_3^2$; we give the analogous criterion on the locus $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution and show that all other strata are fine. The proof is constructive and yields an explicit descent. We prove that the obstruction class is unramified along every divisor of the compactification, that a prime $p\ge 5$ obstructs only if the point reduces modulo $p$ into the closure of one of the two codimension-two loci $\mathcal{L}_1$, $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution, and that $\mathcal{M}_3$ has transverse $A_1$-singularities along both, above which the class ramifies; local densities predict that $\mathcal{L}_2$ is met modulo $p$ with probability $\asymp 1/p$, so that it carries the obstruction. A census of all 214,260,288 rational points of weighted moduli height at most 7 agrees with this mechanism and supports the conjecture that the proportion of fine points tends to zero like $(\log B)^{-1/2}$.

papers.title: The Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence can be arbitrarily non-degenerate in positive characteristic
papers.summary: There is a long tradition of constructing smooth projective varieties in positive characteristic with non-degenerate Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequences. In this paper, we show that for any $n\geq 1$ and any spot $(i, j)$ on the $E_n$-page, except for the cases where the differential is forced to be zero for trivial reasons, there exists a smooth projective variety whose Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence has a non-zero differential with source $E_n^{i, j}$. Our construction is inspired by constructions of nilmanifolds in complex geometry and can be regarded as a positive characteristic analogue.

papers.title: Joint Extension Field Point Counts for Superelliptic Curves
papers.summary: Fix a finite field $\mathbf{F}_q$, an integer $m\ge2$ prime to $q$, and $2\leκ\le m$. For a uniformly chosen $κ$-power-free polynomial $F\in\mathbf{F}_q[x]$ of degree $D$, we determine the limiting joint distribution of the affine point counts of $y^m=F(x)$ over $\mathbf{F}_q,\ldots,\mathbf{F}_{q^n}$ as $D\to\infty$, with $q$ and $n$ fixed. The probability generating function is a finite Euler product with explicit local factors. Equivalently, the limiting vector is a sum of independent closed-point contributions, each of which may affect several extension degrees. We obtain the formula by specializing the equidistribution and motivic Euler product formalism of Bertucci-Howe. We then compute means, covariances, and moment expansions as $q$ varies in a fixed reduced residue class modulo $m$, after the degree limit has been taken. The one-field specialization recovers the power-free affine point-count distribution of Cheong-Wood-Zaman.

papers.title: Effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate distribution for Abelian varieties with applications
papers.summary: We establish a uniform effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimate for abelian varieties, conditional on the Mumford-Tate conjecture and the standard analytic conjectures for L-functions attached to the irreducible representations of the Chebotarev-Sato-Tate group. The proof uses spectral majorants and minorants of indicator functions. For regions whose boundaries have finite upper (d-1)-dimensional Minkowski content, the resulting exponent improves that in Bucur et al. (Theorem 1.1, 2024) whenever the Sato-Tate group has rank greater than one. We establish uniform estimates for regions and finite Galois extensions that vary with the counting parameter, and for prime-dependent regions satisfying an explicit variation condition. As an application, we obtain a conditional upper bound for the number of primes at which a weight-two newform with a quadratic coefficient field has a rational Fourier coefficient. We also formulate a discrepancy conjecture, motivated by a probabilistic model, that implies the asymptotic predicted by Murty (Conjecture 3.4, 1999).

papers.title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
papers.summary: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$. Using Hassett's moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we first show that the generating function of the $S_n$-equivariant Hodge-Deligne polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ is obtained from that of the moduli spaces of minimally weighted pointed curves by plethysm with the explicit symmetric function $Z=h_1-\sum_{k\ge3}(x+x^2+\dots+x^{k-2})h_k$; numerically, this is an explicit change of variables. The latter spaces map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$, and over each boundary stratum they are built from punctured universal curves and Losev-Manin spaces. Combining the stratification by stable graphs with Burnside's formula and twisted characteristics, we obtain in genus two a closed formula whose only non-elementary input is the cohomology of symplectic local systems on $\mathcal M_{1,1}$ and $\mathscr A_2$, known by work of Eichler-Shimura and Petersen. This determines the $S_n$-representations on all $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for $n\le 19$ and on all even degree $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for every $n$. We carry out the computation in all degrees for $n\le 18$, where it agrees with an independent computation by point counts, and in even degrees for $n\le 30$. As an application, we find that the even degree cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ is of Hodge-Tate type if and only if $n\le 20$: the space $H^{23,1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is the multiplicity free $S_{21}$-representation with Frobenius characteristic $s_1\cdot h_2[e_{10}]$, of dimension $1939938$, so that $H^{24}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is not spanned by algebraic cycle classes.

papers.title: On the interpolation property of Kupferer's Lubin-Tate regulator maps
papers.summary: Generalizing both [LZ14] and [ScV26, SaV24] we prove the interpolation property at Artin characters of Kupferer's regulator map [Ku20] over a fixed local field $L$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for $p$ any prime. Since our methods cover the case $p=2,$ we in particular close a gap in the literature even for the (cyclotomic) 2-variable regulator map from [LZ14]. Moreover, we study big (dual) Bloch-Kato exponential maps for unramified towers and we use them to improve Colmez' reciprocity law in the Lubin-Tate setting from [SaV24]. Finally, we compare Kupferer's regulator map with the 2-variable regulator map of Loeffler-Zerbes when $L=\mathbb{Q}_p$.

papers.title: Petersson-rigid lattices of signature (2,1) and their harmonic weak Maass forms
papers.summary: An even lattice $L$ of signature $(2,1)$ is Petersson-rigid if the orthogonal group of its discriminant form acts absolutely irreducibly on the space of cusp forms of weight $\frac32$ for its Weil representation, a space of dimension at least two. We prove, with computer assistance, that there are exactly twelve such lattices up to isometry, and we determine their root bases. Four of them are theta lattices, whose cusp forms are lifts of unary theta series. On each, the space is $\mathbb C F_0\otimesσ_0$ for one form $F_0$ and an irreducible $σ_0$, so the Petersson norm is $\|F\|^2=t_μ\|c_F(μ)\|^2$ for all cusp forms $F$, with one $t_μ>0$, $μ$ the least exponent of $F_0$ and $c_F(μ)$ the coefficient of $q^μ$ in $F$. We prove that the harmonic weak Maass forms of weight $\frac12$ in the $σ_0$-isotypic part with a pole of least possible order are exactly the forms $\mathcal H_F$ with principal part $q^{-μ}\overline{c_F(μ)}$, and $ξ_{1/2}\mathcal H_F=F/t_μ$. For the four theta lattices it is a theorem that $t_μ=\frac{s-1}{12}\sqrt s$, with $s$ the square-free part of $|\det L|/2$, and the $\mathcal H_F$ come from umbral moonshine. For the eight others we compute $F_0$, $t_μ$ and $\mathcal H_{F_0}$: the Hecke eigenvalues are integers and, at the primes computed, the $a_p$ of an elliptic curve, and for three of the eight $F_0$ is explicit as an eta-theta product. papers.title: Universality Criterion Sets for Definite Quadratic Lattices over Polynomial Rings
papers.summary: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $\neq 2$. Under suitable assumptions on the dimensions of anisotropic quadratic forms over $k$ and $k(x)$, we show that a definite integral quadratic form over the polynomial ring $k[x]$ is universal if the form represents all scalars from $k$ and all scalar multiples of $x$. The coefficient field $k$ in our main result can be a finite field, a non-dyadic higher local field, a global function field, or a one-variable function field over $\mathbb{C}$ or $\mathbb{C}(t)$. We have a finite universality criterion set over $k[x]$ for some coefficient fields $k$, including some cases where $k$ has infinitely many square classes (e.g., $k=\mathbb{C}(t)$).

papers.title: Elmendorf's Theorem for $\infty$-categories
papers.summary: Motivated by Teleman's study of gauged topological quantum field theories, our main result is an analog of Elmendorf's theorem in the setting of simplicial group actions on $\infty$-categories. We also show an analog of Whitehead's theorem in this setting.

papers.title: Test ideals can be computed by boundaries
authors: with Appendix joint with Daniel Apsley
papers.summary: Let $R$ be a normal $F$-finite ring of characteristic $p>0$. We show that one effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $Δ$, with $K_R+Δ$ $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$, computes the big test ideal. This answers a question of Schwede and Smith. More generally, we prove their conjecture that test module of a Cartier algebra acting on an ideal is the test module of a single map $ψ$ in the algebra and even the image of $ψ$. We prove a global version for schemes quasi-projective over an $F$-finite local ring as well. In particular, every such normal, locally strongly $F$-regular scheme admits an effective boundary $Δ$ for which $(X,Δ)$ is locally strongly $F$-regular and $K_X+Δ$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$.

papers.title: Existence of Ulrich bundles on polarized surfaces and weakly Ulrich bundles on polarized varieties in positive characteristic
papers.summary: In their seminal paper \cite{eisenbud2003resultants}, Eisenbud and Schreyer asked whether every smooth projective variety admits an Ulrich bundle with respect to each very ample polarization. This question has stimulated extensive research for more than two decades. Recently, Anghel \cite{anghel2026smooth} constructed counterexamples over $\mathbb C$ in dimension two, and Lopez \cite{lopez2026existence} extended this nonexistence result to higher dimensions. In this article, we study the existence problem for sufficiently large multiples of a fixed polarization and derive applications in positive characteristic. Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, we prove that every polarized smooth surface admits an Ulrich bundle and every polarized smooth variety admits a weakly Ulrich bundle. Consequently, the Chow forms of surfaces (resp. varieties) admit linear determinantal (resp. determinantal) representations. Moreover, for every such polarized surface, the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves coincides with that on $(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$.

papers.title: The $6\frac{1}{2}$-functor formalism of Cartier modules
papers.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. We construct a coherent formalism of geometric operations on Cartier modules with coefficients in ind-coherent sheaves on noetherian derived $\mathbb F_p$-schemes. For such a scheme $X$, we consider the stable presentable category $\mathrm{Cart}(X)$ of ind-coherent sheaves $M$ equipped with a structural morphism $F_{*,X}M \to M$, where $F_X$ denotes the Frobenius endomorphism. We construct pushforward functors for arbitrary morphisms and exceptional pullback functors for separated morphisms almost of finite type, together with coherent composition and base-change equivalences. We single out conditions under which these functors admit further adjoints. On derived schemes separated and almost of finite type over $\mathbb F_p$, we construct compatible closed symmetric monoidal structures given by shriek tensor products, and establish which functors are symmetric monoidal. The constructions arise from a general procedure for forming functor formalisms of Cartier objects, using their description as lax limits and the universal properties of span $2$-categories developed by Cnossen--Lenz--Linskens [arXiv:2505.19192].

papers.summary: We consider the problem of constructing maximal curves with few automorphisms over finite fields. Our main ingredient is the determination of the \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\!\left(\overline{\mathbb F}_p\right)\)-stabilizer of the roots of the Chebyshev polynomials, apart from two exceptional cases already treated in the literature. We prove that, in all other cases, the only nontrivial Möbius symmetry is the sign involution. This settles the general case for the automorphism groups of the corresponding Chebyshev curves. We further construct an infinite family of maximal curves of unbounded genus whose only nontrivial automorphism is the hyperelliptic involution. This reveals a contrasting phenomenon to the common heuristic that curves with many rational points tend to have large automorphism groups.

papers.title: On the Torsion Subgroup of the Néron--Severi Group
papers.summary: We prove an explicit bound for the torsion subgroup of the Néron--Severi group of a smooth projective complex variety. As an application, we deduce an explicit bound for the torsion sections of a traceless abelian scheme over a complex curve.

papers.title: On OpenAI's proof of the Nagata conjecture
papers.summary: These notes are an expanded account of my talk at UMass Amherst on OpenAI's remarkably simple proof of the Nagata conjecture. I hope they will be useful, especially to non-experts. The standard reduction to the normal cone and the collision of fat points into one monomial scheme reduce the problem to interpolation of monomial schemes on the normal ruled surface of a smooth plane cubic. The novelty is that the study of the asymptotics of theta functions as the cubic develops a node, together with interpolation duality, reduces the problem further to interpolation on a triangle of lattice points, which is straightforward. The same calculation determines the nef and pseudoeffective cones of a weighted blow-up of ${\Bbb P}^2$ at one point for very general local parameters when the ratio of weights is greater than nine.

papers.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds
papers.summary: We show that all compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact Kähler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.

papers.title: A semiampleness result for hyperkähler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
papers.summary: We give a geometric proof of the following statement: let $X$ be a smooth hyperkähler fourfold such that the Picard group is generated by a line bundle $L$ that is nef, non-trivial, and not big. If the Kodaira dimension of $L$ is non-negative, some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration. The proof requires a number of tools which are of independent interest, including an analogue of Voisin's unobstructedness result and a smoothing result for singular Lagrangian subvarieties.

papers.title: Discrete homotopy of graphs and $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements
papers.summary: Discrete homotopy theory is a combinatorial homotopy theory defined for discrete objects. Barcelo--Severs--White conjectured that the homotopy groups of complements of $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements are isomorphic to the discrete homotopy groups of graphs associated with the Coxeter complexes. We show that this correspondence fails in general by giving a counterexample in degree two for the $4$-parabolic subspace arrangement of type $A_5$.

papers.title: An Arithmetic Property of Intertwining Operators for Real Reductive Groups
papers.summary: Let $G$ be the group of complex points of a connected split reductive group defined over ${\mathbb Q}$. We study the standard intertwining operator between representations parabolically induced from essentially tempered cohomological representations of Levi subgroups of maximal parabolic subgroups. Under certain algebraicity, purity, and criticality hypotheses, the operator is holomorphic and invertible at a particular point of evaluation. The relative Lie algebra cohomology of these induced representations is one-dimensional in the lowest nonzero degree. Under prescribed rational generators of these one-dimensional spaces, we show that the intertwining operator is a nonzero rational multiple of a certain product of ratios of local $L$-factors. This is a cohomological version of Langlands's calculation of the Gindikin-Karplevic formula. The main theorem provides a local input for the arithmetic study of special values of Langlands--Shahidi $L$-functions.

papers.title: Comparison of Logarithmic Hochschild Homologies
papers.summary: We construct a comparison morphism $\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Rog}}\to\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Ols}}$ between Rognes' logarithmic Hochschild homology and Olsson's logarithmic Hochschild homology which generalizes the comparison between Gabber's log cotangent complex $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{Gab}}$ and Olsson's log cotangent complex $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{Ols}}.$ In particular, Olsson's comparison is recovered as the first associated graded piece of our comparison morphism $\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Rog}}\to\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Ols}}.$ In the development of this comparison, we also prove a descent result for the cotangent complex generalizing a result of Bhatt, and construct a notion of HKR completed Hochschild homology for a general morphism of derived stacks which is functorial in the morphism and generalizes existing constructions of Hochschild homology when the base is affine.

papers.title: Mustafin degenerations of six points in the projective plane and self-duality
papers.summary: Mustafin varieties provide a framework for degenerating the projective plane together with marked points, governed by the combinatorics of Bruhat-Tits buildings. Such limit objects are parametrized by the boundary points of a projective compactification of the moduli space of $n$ points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ constructed by Schaffler-Tevelev. In this paper, we study the locus of this compactification generically parametrizing self-dual configurations, or equivalently, six points lying on a conic. We prove that this locus is a tropical compactification of the moduli space of self-dual configurations, with associated fan a refinement of the self-dual tropical Grassmannian introduced by Geiger-Hashimoto-Sturmfels-Vlad. We show that this compactification is a blow up of $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,6}$ and we classify the objects it parametrizes: degenerations of $\mathbb{P}^2$ equipped with a stable $6$-pointed rational curve that records the limiting conic.

papers.title: Relative Hitchin fibrations and endoscopy for Unitary Friedberg--Jacquet varieties
papers.summary: We prove a relative fundamental lemma for the unitary symmetric variety $GL_n(k')\backslash U_{2n}$, proving a conjecture of Leslie, Xiao, and Zhang. Our proof reduces to the Lie algebra and argues over function fields in positive characteristic, using methods from Ngo-Laumon and Ngo. In particular, we reinterpret orbital integrals in terms of the cohomology of relative affine Springer fibers and globalize this using unitary versions of Hitchin moduli spaces for symmetric pairs via a product formula. As the main global input, we prove a matching of perverse sheaves between relative Hitchin moduli spaces and their corresponding endoscopic variants.

papers.title: Linear Complementary Pairs of MDS Codes from Elliptic Curves
papers.summary: In this paper, we investigate the Linear Complementary Pairs (LCPs) of Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes that arise from elliptic curves. We establish geometric conditions for LCPs of elliptic codes and prove that they cannot consist entirely of MDS codes when evaluated over all rational points of the curve. To address this, we construct LCPs of MDS elliptic codes by restricting evaluation divisors to subgroup cosets. We apply this method to obtain explicit infinite families of LCPs of MDS codes over Mordell and supersingular elliptic curves, including large-length constructions over quadratic extensions.

papers.title: Fukaya categories of surfaces with DG coefficients
papers.summary: Given a compact surface $S$ admitting a Liouville form, a finite set $Q \subset S$, a line field on $S$, and a local system of dg-categories on $S \setminus Q$ together with a section of the monodromy functor around each interior $q \in Q$, we construct a Fukaya category. We give examples where such Fukaya categories are quasi-equivalent to derived categories of projective completions of line bundles and of iterated blow-ups of the affine plane; and to wrapped Fukaya categories of cotangent bundles of spheres. We define two versions of the Fukaya category, a topological, which is constructed combinatorially from a full arc system, and a geometric, which includes all Lagrangian branes supported on immersed curves. We prove that the topological category embeds into the geometric category in an essentially unique way. To define Lagrangian branes we develop a generalisation of the Chekanov--Eliashberg algebra incorporating dg-coefficients and wrapping along the boundary.

papers.title: Pointwise to global good reduction problems
papers.summary: Given a smooth proper family of varieties over some $p$-adic field, if (sufficiently many of) the closed fibers have good reduction, does the family as a whole have good reduction? This question is asked and positively answered in recent work of Cadoret-Tamagawa for curves in general, and abelian varieties if the base field has absolute ramification at most $p-1$. In this paper we define a general framework for studying this question, yielding new positive answers for families of K3 surfaces and cubic fourfoulds, again with ramification at most $p-1$. Our strategy is to study several extension properties of moduli spaces and how they transfer under various morphisms. Of particular importance are integral canonical models of Shimura varieties, and whether or not their extension properties are preserved under ramified scalar extension. Additionally, building on earlier counterexamples by Raynaud-Ogus-Gabber and Vasiu-Zink, we show that the ramification assumption is optimal for the result of Cadoret-Tamagawa on families of abelian varieties. This reflects the fact that the extension property of Siegel Shimura varieties no longer holds over a field of absolute ramification at least $p$.

papers.title: The Kodaira dimension and minimal models of $\mathcal{A}_6$
papers.summary: We prove that the moduli space $\mathcal{A}_6$ of principally polarized abelian sixfolds has Kodaira dimension zero, determining the remaining case in the Kodaira classification of the spaces $\mathcal{A}_g$. More precisely, every nonzero scalar Siegel modular form of genus six, weight $k$ and positive boundary order $b$ satisfies $k\geq 7b$, with equality precisely for powers of the weight-fourteen harmonic theta series of Dittmann, Salvati Manni and Scheithauer. The canonical ring is therefore a polynomial ring on one generator of degree two. We also prove numerical dimension zero and construct the unique projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal minimal model. Its Picard number is one and its canonical divisor has order two. The perfect cone compactification is a Mori dream space, and the birational automorphism group of $\mathcal{A}_6$ is trivial. The proof combines normal vanishing on the Prym locus, polar intersections on abelian boundary fibers, and an exact theta calculation. A discrepancy estimate recovers the modular open subset from the minimal model.

papers.title: Obstructions to deforming space curves lying on a complete intersection of quadrics
papers.summary: Let $S=S_{2,\ldots,2}\subset\mathbb P^{n+2}$ be a smooth complete intersection of $n$ quadrics containing a line $E$, where $n\geq 3$, and set $D=(n-1)\mathbf h+E$, where $\mathbf h=[\mathcal O_S(1)]$. We study the deformations of smooth curves $C\in |mD|$ and their obstructions. The linear system $|D|$ defines a birational morphism $f:S\to\overline S$ that contracts $E$ to a point and realizes an unprojection in the sense of Papadakis--Reid. When $n=3$, the surface $S=S_{2,2,2}\subset\mathbb P^5$ is a $K3$ surface and $E$ is a $(-2)$-curve. We prove that the complementary open surface $S\setminus E$ admits first-order infinitesimal deformations in $\mathbb P^5\setminus E$ that are obstructed at the second order. Using these obstructions, we show that, for every sufficiently large $m$ with $\operatorname{char} k\nmid m$, there exists a generically non-reduced irreducible component $W_m$ of the Hilbert scheme $\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^5$ of smooth connected curves in $\mathbb P^5$. Its general member $C$ lies on a complete intersection $S_{2,2,2}$ of three quadrics, satisfies $C\sim mD$, and has $h^0(N_{C/\mathbb P^5})-\dim_{[C]}\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^5=3$. In contrast, when $n>3$, we prove that, for every sufficiently large $m$ with $\operatorname{char} k\nmid m$, the corresponding family of curves in $|mD|$ gives rise to a generically smooth irreducible component of $\operatorname{Hilb}^{sc}\mathbb P^{n+2}$.

papers.title: On the existence of polarized varieties without weakly Ulrich bundles
papers.summary: We give an obstruction to the existence of bundles $\mathcal E$ on a smooth $n$-dimensional polarized variety such that $\mathcal E$ is $a$-regular and ${\mathcal E}^*(K_X+(n+1)H)$ is $b$-regular. In particular, this gives an obstruction to the existence of weakly Ulrich bundles. Using the latter and some recent examples of [A1] in dimension $2$, we prove that for any $n \ge 2$ there exist many smooth $n$-dimensional varieties $X$ with a very ample line bundle $H$, such that there is no weakly Ulrich bundle for $(X,H)$.

papers.title: Landau-Siegel zeros over a base field and effective Brauer-Siegel
papers.summary: Let k be a number field. We prove that for every quadratic extension F/k, every real zero beta of L(s, chi_{F/k}) satisfies (1 - beta) log d_F >= c(k) with an effective constant c(k) > 0, and we deduce (through a reduction of Stark) that the Brauer-Siegel theorem holds effectively and uniformly over all Galois extensions K of k, in the form h_K R_K >= c(k) d_K^{1/2} / ((2 pi)^{[K:Q]} log d_K). Stark's effective cases of the Brauer-Siegel theorem were the fields without quadratic subfields, since the quadratic subfields carried the ineffectivity of Siegel's theorem; over a base field k, the first result removes it. Both rely on a uniform bound for Chebotarev sums. Let K/k be a Galois extension with group G, and suppose S is a subset of G containing the identity. For any prime p of k, let delta_p be the proportion of the primes of K above p whose Frobenius lies in S. Then the sum over Np <= X of delta_p log Np / Np is at most (|S|/|G| + epsilon) log X + O(1), uniformly in K, as soon as X >= d_K^C with C depending only on epsilon and the degree [K:Q]. The proof is Kerr's form of the OpenAI argument, simple vanishing at the points (iota theta)_{iota in S}, with theta in a box in O_K, and Masser's zero estimate. The field enters only through Masser's invariant of the lattice of points, which we compute to be [K:Q]/|S| by averaging over the Galois group of the normal closure. Over Q, the determinant method of Green, Barreto, and Kominers gives sharper Chebotarev bounds, and we explain the comparison.
